hints.title: Full Bitmask Inversion
hints.text: The complement of n is found by inverting every bit within its significant bit length. Inversion is equivalent to exclusive or with a mask composed entirely of 1 bits.

hints.title: Zero Boundary Case
hints.text: When n is 0, its binary representation is 0, whose single-bit complement is 1. Handle this case explicitly or ensure the mask has length 1.

hints.title: Mask Calculation
hints.text: Find the smallest mask of all ones that is greater than or equal to n. Then return the bitwise exclusive or of n with this mask.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting back and forth between string representations of binary digits is unnecessarily slow and allocates unnecessary objects.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pure bitwise mask arithmetic executes in constant memory and logarithmic time with respect to N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that n ^ mask flips bits without string conversion and handle n == 0.
complexity.notes: Bit length of N is at most 32 for standard 32-bit integers.
